## Observed Facts

- **Data Scope:** BGL dataset, all time (2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04), level = FATAL, grouped by component.
- **Total FATAL Log Entries:** 855,195 [E1]
- **KERNEL:** 626,450 Log Entries, about 73% of FATAL [E1]
- **APP:** 228,536 Log Entries, about 27% of FATAL [E1]
- **LINKCARD:** 206 Log Entries [E1]
- **MMCS:** 3 Log Entries [E1]

Two components account for virtually all FATAL Log Entries. The corpus has no Team or owner field. The BGL group-by columns are alert_tag, component, level, and node [E2], so the logs cannot tell us which Team owns each component.

## Hypotheses

- KERNEL and APP are the components a Team Lead should check first, because they hold nearly all FATAL volume. This is based on counts only, not on incidents.
- LINKCARD and MMCS are minor by volume. This does not mean they are unimportant.

## Unknowns

- **Team ownership:** The logs do not record which Team owns KERNEL, APP, LINKCARD, or MMCS. I cannot name the owning Teams from this data.
- **Whether these counts are incidents:** Each count is a Log Entry count. Many entries may come from one event.
- **Trend:** I have not checked whether FATAL volume is growing, steady, or spiking over time.

## Next Step

Send me the component-to-Team mapping (from your ownership catalog or org chart). I will join it to these counts and give you the Team ranking. If you also want to know whether KERNEL's FATAL volume is recurring or a one-off spike, I can run a daily trend next.
